_meta.purpose: Level 2 semantic graph on top of the public synthetic telemetry snapshot. The graph does not store data; tools declare how to access it.
_meta.not_yet_wired: route_solution.json (solver) — entities are marked up in advance, not yet populated with data

get_site_summary.description: Get full passport summary and current telemetry for a specific tower by its ID (site_id). Use when the user asks about a specific tower (e.g., 'show tower X', 'what's up with tower Y').

get_regional_accounting_mismatch.description: Get summary of discrepancies between logistics and accounting (in liters and %). Use to answer questions about losses and financial mismatches.

value.description: Value (e.g., '2025-November' for month or 'South' for region)

get_regional_consumption_calculated.description: Get net fuel consumption calculation based on logistics visits for a specific month. Returns data for all regions.

get_regional_accounting_summary.description: Get summary from accounting (consumption, cost, count of towers) for a specific month, without logistics recalculation.

get_site_historical_analytics.description: Get historical analytics (number of alarms, downtime duration by months) for a specific tower. Use for analyzing incident history.

get_global_summary_report.description: Get global summary report (summary_report) for all issues in the system. Returns ready-made counters. Use to answer questions about global problem statistics.

count_sites.description: Count the number of towers based on conditions — telemetry keys. Pass condition dictionary in filters.

filters.description: Condition dictionary. IMPORTANT: for inequalities (greater/less) ALWAYS pass a nested dictionary: {'field_name': {'operator': 'gt/lt/gte/lte', 'value': number}}.

get_sites_list.description: Get a list of tower data based on conditions — telemetry keys. Pass condition dictionary in filters.

filters.description: Condition dictionary. IMPORTANT: for inequalities (greater/less) ALWAYS pass a nested dictionary: {'field_name': {'operator': 'gt/lt/gte/lte', 'value': number}}.

get_top_sites.description: Get a sorted list (top, maximum, minimum). Use ONLY for analytical queries like 'top 5', 'most problematic tower', 'sort by...'.

top_n.description: REQUIRED. Number of records (e.g., 5 for 'top 5', 1 for 'most...').
